documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up (visit 2026-03-06)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 03/06/2026

Ms. Sears, 35, with Graves disease since early 2025, returns. Over recent months she has felt steadily more worn out, and her muscles feel weak. She is close to 8 kg under her usual weight although she eats large meals and snacks constantly because she is always hungry. She feels overheated even in air-conditioned rooms and sweats all day. At night she feels wired and can't settle; anxiety and restlessness are up. No recent illness, no travel.

Medications: she is not taking anything at present, including the methimazole started in August.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with Hashimoto hypothyroidism, maternal aunt with Graves disease, father with hypertension.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, elementary school teacher.

Exam: afebrile. Pulse 112, regular. BP 128/76. Weight 54.5 kg, BMI 20. Skin warm and moist. Fine tremor of both hands. Reflexes brisk and symmetric throughout. Heart and lungs normal. No proptosis, lid lag or conjunctival change. No leg edema. Thyroid diffusely enlarged, non-tender, without nodules.

Labs: TSH <0.01, free T4 3.8 ng/dL, total T3 240 ng/dL. CBC with differential and liver panel today are normal.

Assessment: Graves disease, uncontrolled, off therapy.

Plan:
1. Restart methimazole at 20 mg daily (two 10 mg tablets).
2. Propranolol 20 mg twice daily for heart rate and tremor.
3. Repeat TSH, free T4 and T3 in about 6 weeks, visit after.
4. We again discussed radioactive iodine and surgery as definitive options; she wants to retry medication first.
5. Reviewed reasons to stop methimazole and call: rash, fever, sore throat, jaundice.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Endocrinology note received; meds reconciled
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Endocrinology note from 3/6 received. Note says she had not been taking methimazole. Old methimazole 10 mg daily entry closed; new methimazole 20 mg daily and propranolol 20 mg BID entered as outside prescriptions. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Check-in call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called after reading the 3/6 endocrine note. She has both prescriptions filled and has taken them every day since Saturday. Heart already feels calmer on propranolol. No rash, fever or sore throat. She has a reminder set on her phone for the methimazole. Encouraged her to keep the 6-week lab appointment. Also overdue for her physical; front desk to call.

documents.title: Refill request - propranolol
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax requesting refill of propranolol 20 mg BID. Prescriber is endocrinology; fax returned to pharmacy with endocrinology's number, and pt notified by portal. No action needed from our side.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up (visit 2026-05-11)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 05/11/2026

Graves disease, two months back on methimazole 20 mg daily with propranolol. She has taken both every day. Palpitations and sweating are much better and she is sleeping through most nights. Appetite settling. No rash, fever, sore throat or itching.

Labs 04/20/2026: TSH <0.01, free T4 2.2 ng/dL, total T3 192 ng/dL.

Exam: HR 82, BP 118/72, weight 56.6 kg. No tremor. Skin normal. Thyroid still enlarged, smooth, non-tender. No eye findings.

Assessment: Graves disease, improving on methimazole.

Plan:
1. Decrease methimazole to 10 mg daily.
2. Stop propranolol.
3. TSH, free T4, total T3 and CBC in 8 weeks; may be drawn at her primary care office with results sent here.
4. Follow-up visit after those results.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Endocrinology note received
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 5/11 endocrinology note and 4/20 labs received. Methimazole changed to 10 mg daily on med list; propranolol removed. They ask for labs in July here if she prefers. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Thyroid labs here?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, endocrinology said I could get my next thyroid blood work done at your office since it's closer. It's supposed to be about 8 weeks after my May visit. Could I come Monday morning?

documents.title: RE: Thyroid labs here?
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Alyssa, yes. The orders from endocrinology are in. You're set for Monday 7/13 at 8:00 for a blood draw. No fasting needed. Keep taking your methimazole as usual that morning.

documents.title: Lab draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Venipuncture right antecubital, one attempt. TSH, free T4, total T3 and CBC with diff per endocrinology orders. Results to be copied to endocrinology.

documents.title: Your thyroid labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good morning Alyssa. Big improvement: free T4 is 1.3, now in the normal range, total T3 is 138, also normal, and TSH is starting to come up at 0.04 (it lags behind the others). Blood count normal. I've sent these to endocrinology, who will decide on the dose. Nice work staying on it.

documents.title: Booking my physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I know I skipped last year's physical. Can I get one in September, early morning if possible?

documents.title: RE: Booking my physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're booked for Tuesday 9/22 at 7:30 am. Your Pap is due this year, so we'll plan to do it at that visit.
